newsitem.title: MACAU: China and Macau police link up against gang war.
newsitem.headline: China and Macau police link up against gang war.

text.p: Police from China and Macau on Tuesday vowed to beef up cooperation after a recent spate of shootings, bombings and arson attacks linked to a turf war between rival "triad" gangs in the Portuguese-ruled territory.
Police from Macau and China's adjacent Guangdong province met for three hours in the enclave on Tuesday and discussed issues including crime-fighting cooperation and marine patrols.
The meeting coincides with a surge in violent crime in Macau, which has recorded 14 gang-related murders so far this year versus 21 for the whole of last year.
Zheng Shaodong, head of the Guangdong police group, said the two sides had agreed to step up border controls.
They also agreed to hold a high level meeting to analyse important security-related issues on Monday in neighbouring Zhuhai city in Guangdong, an official source in Macau said.
Macau shares a 240-metre land border with Zhuhai, and Macau police believe many crimes in the enclave are committed by mainland Chinese.

Gangsters are able to flee the tiny 21-square kilometre territory in about 10 minutes after committing a crime, on foot or by boat, local sources said. Macau's inner harbour is just a few metres from Zhuhai's harbour.
A spokesman for Zhuhai's border inspection office said this month that border patrols had been stepped up to help Macau combat the current wave of violent crime.
Macau, a territory of 455,000 on the south China coast, has been under Portuguese rule for four and a half centuries and is set to return to Beijing's control in 1999.

Shootings, knifings, bombings and arson attacks have rocked the once-sleepy territory in recent months, and police suspect many of the shootings, often performed by motorcylists, are carried out by imported mainland hitmen.
Triad brotherhoods, often with links in China, are believed to be fighting over illegal business linked to Macau's legal casino industry, such as protection rackets.
